mri:abstract.gco:CharacterString: The Survey Area Raster (SARASTER) represents the boundaries of various NASIS Area Types, specifically those that represent soil survey areas, such as, "Country", "Non-MLRA Soil Survey Area" or "Raster Soil Survey Area". "Country" area types are sourced from the State Goil Geographic Database (STATSGO), "Non-MLRA Soil Survey Area" are sourced from the Soil Survey Geographic Database (SSURGO) and "Raster Soil Survey Area" are sourced from the Raster Soil Survey databases (RSS). Each cell value is represented by the integer version of the legend key (LKEY), associating it with the legend table.Digital soil mapping is the production of georeferenced soil databases based on the quantitative relationships between measurements made in the field or laboratory and environmental data (McBratney et al. 2003). This digital soil mapping product represents discrete classes (soil map units) delivered as raster data. Both digital and traditional soil mapping use expert knowledge and a conceptual soil-landscape model as a means for organizing environmental information. McBratney Alex B., Mendonça L. Santos, and Budiman B. Minasny. 2003. “On Digital Soil Mapping.”Geoderma 117, no. 1: 3–52. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0016-7061(03)00223-4. The Raster Soil Survey (RSS) database is a representation of soil survey work completed using digital soil mapping methodologies. Where available, this data represents the most detailed level of soil geographic data developed by the National Cooperative Soil Survey. The associated data represents Raster Soil Survey class data, available in this state. The tabular data represent the soil attributes, and are derived from properties and characteristics stored in the National Soil Information System (NASIS). The spatial data rendered in the geodatabase result from Raster Soil Survey - Project Mapping. Raster Soil Survey is a reference to products of soil survey work completed using digital soil mapping methodologies. The gridded map layer is offered in an ArcGIS file geodatabase raster format. The raster map data have a 10 meter cell size that aligns with the Gridded Soil Survey Geographic (gSSURGO) Database. Raster Soil Survey data represents the most detailed soil survey information for a given area within the Gridded National Soil Geographic Database (gNATSGO) product. Each cell is linked to a map unit identifier called the map unit key. The unique map unit key is used to link to raster cells to mapunit and aggregated attribute tables. Additional information on methods, process and standards for Digital Soil Mapping and Raster Soil Survey can be found in Chapter 5 of the Soil Survey Manual, Part 648 of the National Soil Survey Handbook, and the USDA-NRCS Raster Soil Survey page.

mri:purpose.gco:CharacterString: The Raster Soil Survey (RSS) statewide dataset was created for use in local, state-wide, national, and regional resource planning and analysis of soils data. The dataset consists of soils data in raster format from Digital Soil Mapping (DSM) projects along with associated attribute tables. The raster map layer data can be readily combined with other national, regional, and local raster layers, e.g., National Land Cover Database (NLCD), the National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) Crop Data Layer, or the National Elevation Dataset (NED).

mco:useLimitation.gco:CharacterString: The U.S. Department of Agriculture, Natural Resources Conservation Service, should be acknowledged as the data source in products derived from these data. This dataset is not designed for use as a primary regulatory tool in permitting or siting decisions, but may be used as a reference source. This is public information and may be interpreted by organizations, agencies, units of government, or others based on needs; however, they are responsible for the appropriate application. Federal, State, or local regulatory bodies are not to reassign to the Natural Resources Conservation Service any authority for the decisions that they make. The Natural Resources Conservation Service will not perform any evaluations of these maps for purposes related solely to State or local regulatory programs. Digital data files are periodically updated. Files are dated, and users are responsible for obtaining the latest version of the data.
See access and use constraints information.

mrl:description.gco:CharacterString: Raster Soil Survey datasets are a composite of individual Raster Soil Survey Projects. Each project was prepared using digital soil mapping methodologies, incorporating remotely sensed data and field collected samples. This dataset consists of georeferenced digital map data and computerized attribute data. The soil classes are linked to attributes in the National Soil Information System (NASIS) relational database, which gives the proportionate extent of the component soils and their properties.

mrl:description.gco:CharacterString: The state RSS datasets are compiled and updated using an ArcGIS Pro Python toolbox, Build Raster Soil Survey (RSS) Database.pyt. The Dataset rebuilds the File Geodatabase using current export of tabular data from NASIS, it mosaics in any new mapping from the the MURASTER, PARASTER or adjustments to the SARASTER, and it validates several standards.
